title: Introduce prefetch warmup efficiency meter and dashboard autotuner
author: Luca Hart
description:
Motivation: We observe intermittent cold-path latency spikes and unexpectedly high token cost on first-invocation paths for multi-chunk requests. Root cause analysis (ENG-4521) showed that prefetch jobs often don't fully warm kernel/jit/kv caches for sharded serving, and current dashboards lack a compact signal to quantify effectiveness. This PR introduces a derived metric "prefetch_warmup_efficiency" (ratio of useful warmup hits to prefetch attempts) and an autotune pipeline to recommend warmup batch sizes and backoff windows.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds the metric at the telemetry collector, surfaces warmup tags on spans, exposes a warmup-efficiency dashboard and an autotune job that suggests config changes, and adds an alert that suppresses noisy flaps with hysteresis. Changes are behind a feature flag (observability.prefetch_warmup) and include unit + integration tests and a small Console UI panel.

Checklist:
- [x] implement prefetch_warmup_efficiency gauge and aggregation windows (1m/5m/1h)
- [x] attach warmup_reason and warmup_outcome tags to invocation spans for correlation
- [x] dashboard JSON with heatmap, efficiency sparkline, and recommended tuning panel
- [x] alerting rule: prefetch_warmup_degradation (30m sustained < 0.6 triggers) with auto-suppress for known deployment windows
- [x] autotune job that runs nightly on sampled traffic and posts recommended batch_size/warmup_lookahead to a suggestions index
- [x] unit tests + synthetic replaybench integration test
- [x] feature-flag rollout + docs blurb in changelog

Backward compatibility and rollout: All telemetry additions are additive. The feature is gated; no change to serving defaults. The dashboard and autotune job are opt-in via console toggle. Alert thresholds are conservative and have a 2-hour quiet-window to avoid noisy pages during releases.

Operational notes: The autotune job outputs recommendations with confidence bins; recommendations include an estimated cost delta and expected tail latency impact. We intentionally cap suggested batch_size to prevent regressions on small-tenant traffic. The alerter includes an annotation with the last successful autotune run ID to aid triage.

Testing and verification: Unit tests validate metric computation for synthetic traces. Integration test replays a warmup-heavy synthetic workload and asserts the efficiency metric rises above 0.85 after warmup. CI initially showed a flaky integration test related to timing; I adjusted the replaybench timings and reran CI (see commits).

Related work: builds on the kernel warmup observability hooks from ENG-5012 and reuses the span-tagging primitives introduced in pr-110999 (span warmup tags). Links: Linear: ENG-4521, ENG-5012; Support ticket: SUP-1189.

release_notes: Add prefetch warmup efficiency metric, a warmup-efficiency dashboard, and an autotune job that recommends warmup batch sizing. New alert 'prefetch_warmup_degradation' added with conservative thresholds. Feature is gated behind feature flag observability.prefetch_warmup.
notes_for_sre: When enabling in prod, monitor the suggested batch_size drift and the autotune confidence bins for first 48 hours. The alert includes an annotation for the last autotune run ID. If you see >5% tail latency regressions after applying a recommendation, roll back and file ENG-5012 follow-up.
post_merge_steps: 1) Flip feature flag to staging and run nightly autotune for 3 days. 2) Run warmup-sample query to validate histogram buckets. 3) Add runbook link to alert definition. 4) Schedule a post-deploy review with SRE team.
impact_assessment: Low-risk telemetry addition. Autotune recommendations are suggestions only and require operator apply. No change to runtime defaults. Expected benefit: reduce median cold-path tail by ~10-20% for warmup-sensitive workloads; estimated 3-6% token cost reduction for tenants with heavy multi-chunk patterns.
qa_notes: Replaybench harness included in tests covers main warmup patterns (single-shard, 4-shard, cross-shard). For manual QA, run integration/prefetch_warmup_replay_test.py with --sample-rate=0.1 to replicate high-volume warmup behavior locally.
security_considerations: Autotune writes recommendations to an internal suggestions index accessible only to platform services. No user PII is recorded. Feature flag gate ensures opt-in rollout.
